data.title: King Faisal Specialist Hospital Treats 288 Patients with Genetically Modified T-Cell Therapy
data.content:
Riyadh, November 22, 2026, SPA -- King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre has treated 288 patients using genetically modified T-cell therapy (CAR-T) as of the end of October 2026. Used for certain types of blood cancer, the treatment reflects the hospital's growing clinical expertise in advanced immunotherapies.
    The patients included 251 adults and 37 children, who accounted for approximately 13% of the total. The therapy involves extracting immune cells from a patient's blood, genetically modifying them to recognize and attack cancer cells, and then reinfusing them into the patient's body.
    The hospital's program has made significant advances in both treatment delivery and manufacturing capabilities. It has shifted from relying on international manufacturers to producing the therapy locally. Two patients have already received locally manufactured treatment, following the first dose administered in a Phase I clinical trial in 2025.
    Local manufacturing has reduced the time needed to produce and deliver the treatment from 28 days to less than 14 days. It has also lowered the cost from approximately SAR1.3 million to SAR250,000, a reduction of nearly 80%. These improvements are expected to expand access to advanced treatment and reduce reliance on external manufacturing.
    Developing local manufacturing capabilities is part of the hospital's efforts to localize advanced therapies, in line with the objectives of the National Biotechnology Strategy, which aims to position Saudi Arabia as a global hub for life sciences innovation and the development of advanced biotechnology industries.
    -- SPA
